name: Tubsinte (Tubsinthe), Yelamu winter village at the Candlestick cove
shape_note: Domed/conical tule-thatched family house on a bent-willow pole frame, about 2-6 m across (Milliken 2009 ch.3: 'semi-circular family houses' thatched with tule bundles along marsh edges); houses were burned and rebuilt when dirty. Count and spread are ESTIMATES: the Yelamu numbered c.160-200 people (Milliken 2009) in three seasonal village groups, roughly 6-8 people per house. Largest Yelamu group's winter village (Milliken via Kamiya), believed to be the Crocker Mound CA-SFR-7, ~1/3 mile SW of Candlestick Park off Harney Way, on a sandy terrace facing the bay and a lagoon (first cove north of the county line). Site point approximate. End: Visitacion-group people were baptized at Mission Dolores 1777-85; it may also be one of the two villages burned by the Ssalson on 12 Aug 1776.

name: Temescal (sweat house) at Tubsinte
shape_note: Semi-subterranean sweat house, earth-covered pole-and-thatch dome beside water (BVHP context p.22 on Ohlone temescals). Existence at this village assumed; position estimated.

name: Amuctac, Yelamu summer village in Visitacion Valley
shape_note: Domed/conical tule-thatched family house on a bent-willow pole frame, about 2-6 m across (Milliken 2009 ch.3: 'semi-circular family houses' thatched with tule bundles along marsh edges); houses were burned and rebuilt when dirty. Count and spread are ESTIMATES: the Yelamu numbered c.160-200 people (Milliken 2009) in three seasonal village groups, roughly 6-8 people per house. Summer village of the Tubsinte group 'in nearby Visitacion Valley' (Milliken 2009 App. B; Kamiya). Exact site unknown: placed on Visitacion Creek in the lower valley. End as Tubsinte.

name: Sitlintac, Yelamu winter village at the mouth of Mission Creek
shape_note: Domed/conical tule-thatched family house on a bent-willow pole frame, about 2-6 m across (Milliken 2009 ch.3: 'semi-circular family houses' thatched with tule bundles along marsh edges); houses were burned and rebuilt when dirty. Count and spread are ESTIMATES: the Yelamu numbered c.160-200 people (Milliken 2009) in three seasonal village groups, roughly 6-8 people per house. Winter village of the Chutchui-Sitlintac group (headman Guimas) 'on the shore of the bay just south of AT&T Park' / 'on the shore of Mission Creek' (Milliken; Kamiya). Placed at Steamboat Point (4th & Berry, the 1840s shore); move to the nearest dry sand in the c.1800 land cover if needed. Burned by the Ssalson on 12 Aug 1776 (Palou); a few families camped at the beach again in late 1776.

name: Temescal (sweat house) at Sitlintac
shape_note: Earth-covered sweat house beside the creek. Existence at this village assumed; position estimated.

name: Chutchui, Yelamu summer village on Mission (Dolores) Creek
shape_note: Domed/conical tule-thatched family house on a bent-willow pole frame, about 2-6 m across (Milliken 2009 ch.3: 'semi-circular family houses' thatched with tule bundles along marsh edges); houses were burned and rebuilt when dirty. Count and spread are ESTIMATES: the Yelamu numbered c.160-200 people (Milliken 2009) in three seasonal village groups, roughly 6-8 people per house. Seasonal village 'within a few hundred yards of the mission' (Milliken 2009 p.97), next to the lagoon where the Spaniards pitched 15 tents in June 1776 (Palou). Exact site unknown: placed on the creek (18th St line) between the first (Camp/Albion) and the present mission sites. Its people joined the mission from 1777 (first adult convert Chamis of Chutchui, 24 Jun 1777); headman Guimas baptized 2 May 1784.

name: Petlenuc, Yelamu village at the Presidio bay shore (Crissy Field)
shape_note: Domed/conical tule-thatched family house on a bent-willow pole frame, about 2-6 m across (Milliken 2009 ch.3: 'semi-circular family houses' thatched with tule bundles along marsh edges); houses were burned and rebuilt when dirty. Count and spread are ESTIMATES: the Yelamu numbered c.160-200 people (Milliken 2009) in three seasonal village groups, roughly 6-8 people per house. Third family cluster 'near the beach area facing the sea and the Golden Gate' (Milliken 2009 App. B). NPS archaeology: two food-processing camps at Crissy Field, one just east of the marsh near the beach and one under Sports Basement (Kamiya). Font (28 Mar 1776) saw 'a little hut with four small children' on this beach. Count is an estimate; spread covers both camps.

name: Founding camp of the Anza colonists at Laguna de los Dolores (15 tents)
shape_note: Moraga's party (c.75 people, 286 cattle) arrived 27 Jun 1776 and 'set up fifteen tents near a lagoon' beside Chutchui (Palou, in Milliken 2009 p.95); first mass under a brush arbor (enramada) 29 Jun. Most moved to the Presidio site on 26 Jul; six soldiers and the padres stayed until the timber buildings were ready (mission dedicated 9 Oct 1776). Tent size estimated.

name: First Mission San Francisco chapel and padres' quarters (palisade), first site
shape_note: Timber palisade (palo parado) chapel with living quarters, thatched; built Aug-Oct 1776 by soldiers and San Carlos sailors; a larger second palisade chapel was finished on the same site in 1782; site abandoned when Palou moved the mission to its present site in 1783 (Geiger, in MDNA HCS pp.25-26). Official dimensions 18 x 5 varas (~15 x 4 m) (Market & Octavia HCS p.22). LOCATION DISPUTED: State Historical Landmark 327-1 marker at Camp & Albion (used here); Hendry & Bowman put it near 14th & Mission. NOTE: overlaps the church modeller's scope - drop if already modelled.

name: Stockade around the first mission
shape_note: Palisade fence enclosing the first chapel and dwellings (MDNA HCS p.25: 'surrounded by a stockade for protection'). Draw as a fence outline, not a solid block. Size estimated.

name: Cattle corral of the first mission
shape_note: Corral built by Palou's men near the first chapel (MDNA HCS p.25). Post-and-rail/brush fence; draw as an outline. Position and size estimated.

name: Neophyte tule huts at the first mission site
shape_note: Converts lived in traditional huts until the early 1790s (MDNA HCS p.26). Vancouver (1792) describes mission huts of willow poles and tule, about 12 ft high and 6-7 ft across (Bancroft i.714). Mission Indian population 32 (1777) -> 215 (1783) (Milliken 2009 Table F1). Count estimated (~6 per hut).

name: Neophyte tule huts at the present mission (before the adobe rancheria)
shape_note: Huts of willow poles, twig basketwork and tule/grass thatch, ~12 ft high and 6-7 ft in diameter (Vancouver 1792, Bancroft i.714), replaced by adobe row-houses 1793-1806. Mission Indian population 260 (1784), 622 (1792), 872 (1795) (Milliken 2009 Table F1); unmarried women slept in the monjerio. Count estimated; placed where the rancheria later stood.

name: Neophyte rancheria, adobe row-house range 1 of 8
shape_note: Attached one-room adobe family houses (~20 ft wide, ~10 ft high, one door, one window, clay-tile roof (Webb 1998, via MDNA HCS)) in long parallel ranges: 19 houses built 1793, 20 more 1794, enough for most married neophytes by 1798, and 'eight long rows' 100 yards from the mission by 1806 (Langsdorff, Bancroft ii.131); ~100 cabins in a rectangle of 10 blocks cut by 4 parallel streets and 1 cross street in 1817 (Roquefeuil). Site: across Dolores St from the church (Notre Dame Plaza, 347 Dolores, still an archaeological site; Ambro 2003). RECONSTRUCTED LAYOUT: row positions, orientation (parallel to the Dolores St line), length (12 houses) and the start/end of each row are estimates; the population fell from ~1,000 (1820) to ~250 after the 1823 transfers and the empty houses decayed (Beechey 1826); the last rows were occupied by remaining Indians into the 1840s.

name: Mission Dolores convento (padres' house), later the Mansion House
shape_note: One-storey adobe range with a front corridor, attached to the north side of the church and fronting the road (Dolores St): 'the church ... joins the house of the missionaries' (Choris 1816); 'a solid line' of church, fathers' lodging, storehouses and guard houses (Roquefeuil 1817). Thatched until tile roofs were completed in 1795 (Bancroft i.714). After 1834 part became an inn/tavern - the Mansion House (operating in 1850) - and part a two-storey wooden rectory; Mormon families lodged in mission buildings in 1846. Razed by 1876 for the brick church (now the Basilica site). Length/depth ESTIMATED; start date estimated (contemporary with the 1791 church).

name: Mission quadrangle: north range (1795 adobe building, 180 ft)
shape_note: 'In 1795 another adobe building 180 feet long was erected' (Bancroft i.714). Behind the padres' dwelling 'a large court surrounded by buildings in which the neophytes were employed, chiefly ... wool and weaving' (Langsdorff 1806); Choris (1816): twenty looms, two mule-powered mills. Placed as the north side of a ~40 m court west of the convento; this falls on today's 16th St, which was cut through the mission grounds in 1889. Position/orientation ESTIMATED.

name: Mission quadrangle: west range (1794 tile-roofed storehouse, 150 ft)
shape_note: 'In 1794 a new storehouse 150 feet long was built and roofed with tiles' (Bancroft i.714); granaries, workrooms and probably the monjerio (dormitory for unmarried women, documented by Hendry & Bowman via Market & Octavia HCS p.23) lined the court. Position/orientation ESTIMATED; material of unoccupied buildings was being carried off by 1844 (Bancroft iv.669).

name: Mission escolta (guard) houses
shape_note: Houses 'little different from huts of the Indians, intended for the detachment of guards' in the line with church, padres' house and storehouses (Roquefeuil 1817); the guard was four soldiers in the 1790s (Bancroft i.694). After secularization 'the soldiers barracks was partially demolished and a house constructed on the remains' (Dean, in MDNA HCS p.30). Position ESTIMATED (north end of the line).

name: Mission workshops: tallow and soap house, smithy, carpenter and cabinet shops, tannery, magazines
shape_note: Langsdorff (1806) inspected 'buildings for melting tallow and making soap, smiths' shops, and shops for carpenters and cabinet-makers, magazines for storing tallow, soap, butter, salt, wool, and hides, with storehouses filled with grain' (Bancroft ii.131). The 1853 US Coast Survey shows buildings in the block 15th-16th / Dolores-Guerrero (MDNA HCS note 83); after 1834 a tannery was rebuilt as a residence. Count, sizes and start date ESTIMATED.

name: Mission grist mills (molino), mule-powered
shape_note: 'Two mills moved by mule-power' (Choris 1816); 'two mills' (Engelhardt via Market & Octavia HCS); one molino was converted into a residence after secularization (Dean, MDNA HCS p.30). Position and size ESTIMATED.

name: Mission outbuildings between 14th and 15th Streets
shape_note: 'Several long, narrow rectangular buildings in the blocks between Dolores and Guerrero Streets and 14th and 15th Streets ... not oriented toward the street and ... on land where the Mission had a number of outbuildings' (1874 map; MDNA HCS note 84). Function unknown (storehouses?). Dates ESTIMATED.

name: Mission milking sheds on Dolores Creek
shape_note: 'The milking sheds for the cows were located along Dolores Creek at what is today Mission High School' (Cleary, FoundSF). Construction (adobe, brush or timber) unknown; dates ESTIMATED (operations ended with secularization).

name: Mission pasture wall between Potrero Nuevo and Potrero Viejo (along Precita Creek)
shape_note: Adobe or stone wall built by mission Indians to stop cattle drifting from the Potrero Nuevo to the Potrero Viejo; 'some early accounts place the largest along the north side of Precita Creek, extending east to the northwest corner of the Islais Creek estuary, following the present-day alignment of Cesar Chavez Boulevard'; deteriorated by the early 1850s (BVHP context pp.24-25). Modelled as a straight wall from Cesar Chavez & Mission to Cesar Chavez & Potrero Ave; point = its CENTRE. Dates and exact line ESTIMATED.

name: Mission pasture wall along the southwest foot of Potrero Hill
shape_note: 'Early American maps show another wall running along the southwest side of Potrero Hill, between the headwaters of Mission Creek and Precita Creek' (BVHP context p.25). Approximated by the Potrero Ave line from 17th St to Cesar Chavez St; point = its CENTRE. ESTIMATED.

name: Bateria de Yerba Buena (San Jose battery) at Point San Jose / Black Point
shape_note: Battery ordered April 1797, almost finished June 1797: 'hastily constructed of brushwood fascines for the most part, with eight embrasures and five eight-pound guns', enclosed by a palisade; no garrison, visited daily by a sentinel (Bancroft i.701-702). A Nov 1804 storm levelled the palisade; in 1806 'not even a hut for the gunners' and the guns useless; nothing heard of it in 1811-20 (Bancroft ii.127-128, 372). MATERIAL: earth-and-fascine earthwork, NOT adobe brick. Point = the 'Black Point Fortifications (1797-1909)' site in OSM (Fort Mason, McDowell Rd); footprint estimated.

name: Briones-Miramontes family adobe at El Polin Spring
shape_note: Stone foundation of an adobe house found 2003 by Barbara Voss (Stanford) at El Polin Spring, Tennessee Hollow; Juana Briones lived here c.1815-1830; the Briones and Miramontes families farmed the spring valley (Presidio gardens, a dam south of the spring) and were evicted by the US Army in the early 1850s. Native Californians lived alongside them (lithics). Size ESTIMATED.

name: Miramontes family adobes at El Polin
shape_note: 'Here, at El Polin, Marcos Briones and the Miramontes family all constructed homes' (Presidio archaeology tour 2001, stop 5). Number, positions and dates ESTIMATED.

name: Kiln at El Polin
shape_note: Kiln found just north of the adobe residence (Presidio Trust/Stanford excavations). Form and size ESTIMATED.

name: Timber house built by Russian sailors for Juana Briones, near El Polin
shape_note: 'It is said that Russian sailors constructed a timber house for Juana Briones near here' (Presidio tour 2001); J. R. Sanchez also mentions houses 'built of timber by the Russians' at El Polin (Bancroft iii.709 n.). Legend-grade; dates and position ESTIMATED.

name: Apolinario Miranda house at the Ojo de Agua de Figueroa
shape_note: Miranda (Juana Briones's husband) had built a house at the spring before obtaining the 100-vara grant 'Ojo de Agua de Figueroa' (1833/1838); the spring 'is near the middle of Lyon street, between Vallejo and Green' (Eldredge ii.525; Bancroft iii.712). Material, size and end date ESTIMATED (Miranda d.1847).

name: Jose Cornelio Bernal adobe (Rancho Rincon de las Salinas y Potrero Viejo)
shape_note: Bernal never lived on his rancho; 'his primary residence was an adobe located on Duncan Street between San Jose Avenue and Valencia Street' (BVHP context p.26, after Olmsted 1979). Bernal moved to San Francisco by 1833, ran cattle from the mid-1830s, grant 1839. Dates, size, orientation ESTIMATED.

name: Bernal's cattle corral (diseno of Rancho Rincon de las Salinas)
shape_note: The diseno shows a corral 'in the gap between Mt. St. Joseph and Candlestick Hill'; the only structure Bernal is known to have built on the rancho; gone after the 1860s (BVHP context pp.25-26). Draw as a fence outline. Position estimated (gap north of Bayview/Candlestick Hill along today's Third St).

name: Jose de Jesus Noe's farmhouse on Rancho Las Camaritas
shape_note: Noe was granted Las Camaritas (300 varas square, near 14th-15th & Mission, on Mission Creek) on 21 Jan 1840 and built 'a wood house near the intersection of Fourteenth and Mission streets' (Hendry & Bowman via Market & Octavia HCS p.24); small farm with grain and produce. Size and end ESTIMATED.

name: Noe adobe at the Mission (near Centre/16th Street)
shape_note: Noe's will (1862) leaves his wife 'the adobe house and the Solar on which it stands, near Centre Street (16th St.) at the Mission', plus a frame building and a wooden house on Centre St (FoundSF, Rancho San Miguel Disappears). Position on 16th St and dates ESTIMATED.

name: Noe adobe, Rancho San Miguel
shape_note: 'The original Noe adobe house was in the vicinity of the present-day intersection of 23rd Street and Douglass Street' (Wikipedia, Noe Valley). Rancho San Miguel (one league) granted Dec 1845; Noe sold most of it to Horner in 1854. Size and dates ESTIMATED.

name: Francisco Guerrero adobe at the Mission
shape_note: Guerrero (sub-prefect, alcalde) and his father-in-law De Haro lived at Mission Dolores (Eldredge ii.534); Hendry & Bowman identify a Guerrero adobe near the mission (MDNA HCS p.27); 214-220 Dolores (west side, 15th-16th) were part of the Guerrero grant. Position and dates ESTIMATED.

name: Francisco de Haro adobe at the Mission
shape_note: De Haro (first alcalde 1835, owner of Laguna de la Merced from 1837, d.1849) lived at the Mission; Hendry & Bowman list a De Haro adobe near the mission (MDNA HCS p.27). Position UNKNOWN (placed near the Guerrero house); dates estimated.

name: Candelario Valencia adobe at the Mission
shape_note: Valencia received lots at Mission Dolores from Guerrero (50 varas, 18 Nov 1840) and Alvarado (100 varas, 18 May 1841) (Dwinelle, Addenda; US v. Candelario Valencia); Valencia St is named for him. House position UNKNOWN; dates estimated.

name: Californio adobe and frame houses of the pueblo of Dolores (unlocated)
shape_note: 'Between 1835 and ... 1848 ... a number of new adobe and wood-frame houses were constructed in the Mission Dolores area, generally by Californio families'; 'by the 1850s, there were more than 50 adobe buildings in the Mission Dolores district'; by 1850 the community spread from 14th to 19th St and from Mission to Church St (Dean, in MDNA HCS p.30). About half of the peninsula's c.300 people lived here in 1845 (Bancroft iv.662). Count ESTIMATED.

name: Galindo / De Haro rancho house and corral at Laguna de la Merced
shape_note: Jose Antonio Galindo was granted Laguna de la Merced on 23 Sep 1835 (a Mexican grant required a house within a year); he 'did little to develop' it and sold it to Francisco de Haro on 12 May 1837 for 100 cows and $25 in goods; De Haro lived at the Mission. NO SOURCE LOCATES A BUILDING: placed on the lake's east shore as a placeholder.

name: Juana Briones adobe at North Beach (Powell & Filbert)
shape_note: 'In 1836 Juana Briones ... built an adobe house on the westerly side of Telegraph hill, where now Powell and Filbert streets cross ... For years it was the only house between Yerba Buena and the presidio'; small farm supplying milk and eggs to ships (Eldredge ii.524; Bancroft iii.709 n.). Thomes (1843): 'a large adobe house, and outbuildings'. Size and end ESTIMATED (she moved to Rancho La Purisima from 1844 but kept the property).

name: Juana Briones corral and dairy yard (Washington Square)
shape_note: Washington Square 'occupies the land that once served as her corral and dairy farm' (FoundSF, Juana Briones). Draw as a fence outline with sheds. Size ESTIMATED.

name: William A. Richardson's tent - first structure of Yerba Buena
shape_note: June 1835: 'a canvas tent stretched on pine posts' (Eldredge ii.500) - Dana's 'shanty of rough boards' of Dec 1835 - on Richardson's 100-vara lot fronting the Calle de la Fundacion (later Dupont/Grant), block Dupont-Stockton-Clay-Washington, 'near the corner of Dupont and Clay' (Bancroft iii.709). Rotation: the lot fronted the diagonal Calle de la Fundacion (estimated).

name: Richardson's adobe 'Casa Grande'
shape_note: Adobe, 'one and a half stories high', on the site of the tent, west side of Dupont between Washington and Clay (later Adelphi Theatre site); built 1837 (Eldredge, Bancroft; Annals says 1838); stood diagonally to the later grid (Eldredge ii.519). One of the largest buildings in town in 1846-8: Paty & McKinley store 1843-5, receptor's office 1844, Mormon winter quarters and meeting house 1846-7, Parker's store 1847-8; the only pre-1847 building left near the plaza in 1851; taken down May 1852. Size ESTIMATED. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Temescal of Richardson's Indian boatmen at the Laguna Dulce
shape_note: 'In 1835 Captain Richardson's Indians had a temescal on the flat at the foot of Sacramento street where, after heating themselves in the sweat house, they plunged into the waters of the Laguna Dulce' (Eldredge ii.514). End ESTIMATED.

name: Jacob P. Leese's house (first house of Yerba Buena)
shape_note: Frame house 'sixty feet long and twenty-five feet broad', boards landed 2 Jul and finished by 10 am on 4 Jul 1836 for the first Independence Day celebration in California (Annals 168-170); 100-vara lot adjoining Richardson's on the south, later the St. Francis Hotel site at the SW corner of Clay & Dupont. Not known to have been used after Leese moved to the beach; 'perhaps removed about 1840'; gone by 1846 (Bancroft v.680). End ESTIMATED.

name: Leese's beach store / Hudson's Bay Company post / Mellus & Howard / United States Hotel
shape_note: Large frame store and dwelling on the west line of Montgomery between Sacramento and Clay, at the later Commercial St (Annals 171; Eldredge ii.507). Sold Aug 1841 to the HBC: 'about thirty by eighty feet with a big hall in the middle', store on one side, dwelling on the other, four bedrooms behind, kitchen at the back (Mrs Rae); 'built of wood, shingled ... of the old-fashioned Dutch form' (Peirce 1841); 'a large two-story frame building' (Brown). Mellus & Howard 1846-9; United States Hotel 1849-50; burned 14 Jun 1850. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Kitchen of the Leese / HBC store
shape_note: 'Adjoining it, in '39, a small kitchen' (Bancroft v.679). Size estimated.

name: Hudson's Bay Company stable / warehouse (adobe)
shape_note: Rae 'built an additional structure south of the kitchen in '42, used at first for a stable, and later as a warehouse; advertised as a warehouse at cor. Sac. and Montgom. streets in '47' (Bancroft v.679); Brown calls it 'an adobe ware-house'. Size estimated.

name: HBC warehouse on the beach (later Larkin's 'little white house under the hill')
shape_note: W. H. Davis: the HBC 'built a kind of warehouse' on the beach lot east of Montgomery in '42-3, still standing in '47-8; Bancroft supposes it is Larkin's beach house rented as a store in 1847-8 (v.679). Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: 'Kent Hall' - ship's deckhouse from the bark Kent
shape_note: Nathan Spear bought from Capt. Steele of the bark Kent 'a ship's house twelve by eighteen feet' early in 1838 and placed it near the beach at the NW corner of Clay and Montgomery (Eldredge ii.507); later a sleeping room; stood till after 1848 (Bancroft v.681). End ESTIMATED. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Nathan Spear's store (later W. H. Davis's, 'No. 2 Montgomery St')
shape_note: Wooden store built '38-9 'just north of Kent Hall and farther back from Montgomery St'; Spear lived and traded here till 1846, then W. H. Davis to 1849, when it was removed for a new building (Bancroft v.681). Size estimated. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Spear & Hinckley grist mill (mule power) - first in California
shape_note: 'A 2-story heavy frame building for a mill run by mule power', Daniel Sill builder and miller, machinery from Callao 1839; north side of Clay between Montgomery and Kearny, about 15 ft back from Clay; Mofras (1841) saw four mules working a flour mill, bolting machine and saw-mill together; storehouse from 1846; Cross, Hobson & Co. 1848 (Eldredge ii.530-531; Bancroft v.681). Brown says Parker's new two-storey store of March 1848 stood on 'the Old Mill House' lot. Size estimated. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: William S. Hinckley adobe (alcalde Bartlett's office 1846-47)
shape_note: Adobe built 1840 on the north half of the Spear-Hinckley corner lot, next to Spear's store; Hinckley lived here till his death in 1846; Alcalde Bartlett used it as office and residence; leased to Ward & Smith 1847; 'stood on what is now the southwest corner of Montgomery and Merchant streets and was removed in 1850 to make way for the Naglee building' (Eldredge ii.517). Size estimated. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Juan (John) Fuller's three small wooden houses and adobe bake oven
shape_note: Fuller (English butcher and cook, in California from 1823) put up three small wooden dwellings in 1839 near the middle of his 100-vara lot on Kearny between California and Sacramento (Eldredge ii.515; Bancroft v.678; Brown: 'two small frame houses and an adobe bake oven'); Leidesdorff kept store in the southern one 1845-7. Sizes and end estimated. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Fuller's wash-house at the spring at the foot of Clay Street
shape_note: 'At the foot of Clay street a spring of good water flowed from under the bank and supplied the ships. Here in 1838-9 Juan Fuller had a washhouse' (Eldredge ii.514; Bancroft v.681). End ESTIMATED.

name: Francisco Caceres adobe (SE corner Dupont & Pacific)
shape_note: Ex-sergeant of dragoons Caceres obtained a 100-vara lot in March 1838 and built an adobe 'on what is now the southeast corner of Dupont and Pacific', living there till 1844 or later (Eldredge ii.515; Bancroft v.684). End ESTIMATED. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: A. B. Thompson's hide house at Buckelew's Point
shape_note: 'In 1838, A. B. Thompson built a hide house at Buckalew's Point at the head of a little cove, near the northeast corner of Sansome and Pacific streets' (Eldredge ii.515); accessible to boats at high tide; remembered 1838-9 and 1846-8 (Bancroft v.684-5). Size, material and end ESTIMATED.

name: John Calvert Davis house
shape_note: English ship-carpenter and blacksmith; granted a 100-vara lot on Kearny between Washington and Jackson in 1839 and built a house on Washington St near the southeast corner of the lot (Eldredge ii.515-516); R. M. Sherman rented it late 1848. Size and end estimated. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: J. C. Davis carpenter and blacksmith shop
shape_note: 'Back of it a carpenter and blacksmith shop' (Eldredge ii.516); blacksmiths Walcott (1847) and Rose & Reynolds (1847-8) succeeded him (Bancroft v.683). Size estimated.

name: Victor Prudon adobe (near SW corner Montgomery & Pacific)
shape_note: 'Near the southwest corner of Montgomery and Pacific streets, Victor Prudon built an adobe house in 1839' (Eldredge ii.516); Sutter (1839) and Mofras (1841, 'occupied by Mathurin') mention it; Bancroft could not locate it (v.684). End ESTIMATED.

name: Carlos Glein blacksmith shop
shape_note: 'From about '45 Carlos Glein had a blacksmith-shop, and perhaps a residence, on his lot' (Bancroft v.684, block 35 lot 6). Size, material and end estimated. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Vioget house / Portsmouth House (first hotel), SE corner Clay & Kearny
shape_note: Jean Vioget (surveyor of 1839) put up a wooden building in 1840-1 where he lived and kept a bar and billiard saloon; Ridley 1844-6; John H. Brown turned it into a hotel and named it the Portsmouth House in July 1846; E. P. Jones's hotel 1847-8; 'a small cluster of one-story buildings' (Piper). Eldredge ii.518-520; Bancroft v.680. End ESTIMATED (fire of 14 Jun 1850). Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: John Cooper ('Jack the sailor') shanty and groggery
shape_note: 'On the Jackson street lot just below Dupont, his cousin, John Cooper, alias "Jack the sailor," built a shanty and kept a groggery' (1840; Eldredge ii.517); Hiram Teal's store to 1843 (Bancroft v.683); Brown: small frame house where the 1848 Goat Island negotiation took place. End estimated. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Jose Antonio Ortega shanty (near Pacific & Powell)
shape_note: 'Near the S.E. cor. of Pacific and Powell, in a little depression, Davis remembers that Jose Antonio Ortega had a little shanty house in '38-41' (Bancroft v.684). Size estimated.

name: Shanty of Jacinto (a Lascar)
shape_note: 'At c there was another shanty, said to have been occupied by a Lascar named Jacinto in '39-47' (Bancroft v.683, block 31). Position within the block unknown. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Peter Sherreback house (SE corner Washington & Kearny)
shape_note: Danish settler; 50-vara lot granted 1842, wooden house built 1843 (Eldredge ii.525; Bancroft v.682); 'This gave way to the El Dorado gambling house' of 1849. Size estimated. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Capt. John Paty's shanty and fence on the Sanchez lot
shape_note: 'Capt. Paty in '44-5 bought the Sanchez 100-vara lot, fenced it, and built a shanty' (Bancroft v.683). Position within the lot unknown. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Benito Diaz adobe (Ellis boarding house and groggery)
shape_note: 'In 1844 Benito Diaz built an adobe house on the east side of Montgomery street, between Jackson and Pacific, near the lagoon'; sold 1847 to Alfred J. Ellis (boarding house, groggery); a 23-ft well beside it (the drowned-Russian-sailor whisky story) (Eldredge ii.531). End estimated. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Two small adobes on the Diaz-Mesa lot (Jackson St)
shape_note: Piper mentions two small adobes, one unfinished, in 1847; Davis: one begun 1843-4 by Diaz and never finished, the other built by John Cooper about 1844 (Bancroft v.684, block 35 lot 2). Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Adobe shanty of Escalante and Ramirez
shape_note: 'An adobe shanty, occupied in '45-8 by Escalante and Ramirez' (Bancroft v.684, block 35). Position in the block unknown.

name: John Finch ('John Tinker') saloon, bowling alley and blacksmith shop
shape_note: Built 1844-5 on the NW corner of Kearny and Washington (later Wright & Co.'s Miners' Bank and the Bella Union); 'quite a large frame' (Eldredge ii.531; Bancroft v.683; Brown 9a: blacksmith shop and liquor saloon 1845). Size estimated. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Mexican Custom House (the 'old adobe') on the plaza
shape_note: Begun summer 1844, completed Sept 1845, mostly by Indian labour with tiles and timber from the ruined presidio: 'adobe, with tile roof, one story and an attic, fifty-six and a half feet long by twenty-two feet wide, with a veranda six feet wide running across the front and both ends', four rooms; 'on the northwest corner of the plaza ... its front to the plaza and its north end on Washington street' (Eldredge ii.529-530; Bancroft iv.669-670). US flag raised on the pole in front 9 Jul 1846; then barracks, alcalde's and revenue offices; destroyed in the fire of 4 May 1851. Footprint excludes the 1.8 m veranda.

name: Jail adjoining the Custom House
shape_note: 'Adjoining the custom-house there was a jail built later'; on Swasey's 1846-7 view and remembered by Clark, not by Davis or Gillespie (Bancroft v.682). Size, material and dates ESTIMATED.

name: First public school house (Public Institute), Portsmouth Square
shape_note: Small wooden school house built late 1847 'on the south-west corner of Portsmouth Square, fronting on Clay street where it is now joined by Brenham Place' (Annals 677); school opened 3 Apr 1848 (Thomas Douglas); also town hall, court, church and jail; demolished by order of the city in 1850 (Annals 679). Size estimated.

name: Stephen Smith house - Sam Brannan's home and California Star office (SE cor. Dupont & Washington)
shape_note: Smith of Bodega built a wooden house on this 50-vara lot in 1845-6 and leased it in 1846 to Brannan, who lived there and published the Star (first issue 9 Jan 1847) until Feb 1848; then Gillespie (Eldredge ii.533; Bancroft v.682). Size and end estimated. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Jesus Noe's house and alcalde's office (NE cor. Dupont & Clay)
shape_note: 'Noe, the last alcalde under Mexican rule, lived on the northeast corner of Dupont and Clay streets' (Eldredge ii.534); wooden house on his own lot (granted 1843) in 1846-8 (Bancroft v.682; Brown 7a). Start, size and end estimated. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: City Hotel (Leidesdorff adobe, 'Brown's Hotel'), SW corner Clay & Kearny
shape_note: Large adobe built by Leidesdorff: first floor finished Jun 1846, bar and billiard rooms opened 15 Jul 1846, upper part finished Mar 1847; 'The frontage of this house was one hundred and thirty-seven feet, with a wing of sixty feet at each end' (Brown 20b) - i.e. a U with the main range along Clay facing the plaza and wings running back; 'a low building with a veranda in front' (Bancroft v.680). Opened as Brown's Hotel 1 Nov 1846; headquarters of the gamblers 1848-9; destroyed in the fire of 4 May 1851. Footprint = bounding box of the U.

name: Vioget's adobe residence (NW cor. Sacramento & Kearny)
shape_note: 'The adobe house at c was built in '46 by Vioget on the Benavides lot, V.'s wife being a Benavides, and occupied by him in '47-8' (Bancroft v.680); Brown 21b: small adobe, family residence. End estimated. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Grimes family two-storey wooden house
shape_note: 'A small two-story wooden house where the Grimeses lived in '47-8, and where Capt. G. died'; perhaps built by Vioget in '46 (Davis, in Bancroft v.680). Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Vicente Miramontes wooden house (Sacramento St)
shape_note: 'Vicente Miramontes built on his own lot about '44 a wooden house, in which he lived with his family to '48 and later' (Bancroft v.680; Brown 32c: sold to Leidesdorff). Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Padilla residence and two other buildings opposite the school house
shape_note: 'Swasey has a group of 3 buildings here, one of them the residence of Padilla'; Pettet's glassware store 'opposite the school-house' (Apr 1848) (Bancroft v.680). Dates estimated. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: US Navy log blockhouse (NW cor. Dupont & Sacramento)
shape_note: After a false alarm in summer 1846, Lt. Misroon's sailors 'constructed a log blockhouse at or near the northwest corner of Dupont and Sacramento streets on which was mounted a large Spanish gun from the presidio'; later a prison (Eldredge ii.544; Brown 41) and Capt. Hull's hospital shed (Bancroft v.680). Size and end estimated.

name: Leidesdorff's warehouse on the beach (California & Leidesdorff)
shape_note: 'In 1844 or '45 he erected a warehouse on the beach at the foot of California street at what was afterwards the corner of California and Leidesdorff streets' (Eldredge ii.527); US quartermaster's warehouse; S. H. Williams & Co. store 1849 (Bancroft v.678). Size and end estimated.

name: Small landing pier at Leidesdorff's warehouse
shape_note: 'There was a small pier, or wharf, at the landing near the building' (Bancroft v.678); 'a small wharf for landing at high tide' (Eldredge ii.576). Length ESTIMATED; deck height above sea level.

name: Ridley adobe / Leidesdorff cottage and garden (SW cor. Montgomery & California)
shape_note: 'A low one-story bungalow of adobe with a long piazza fronting the bay', twenty varas back from both streets and standing diagonally like Richardson's casa grande (Eldredge ii.518); Bancroft: 'a mixed structure of wood and mud', built '46. Leidesdorff bought it early 1847 and died there May 1848; 'the only house in town which had a garden'; then Howard and Capt. Folsom. Rotation 36 = diagonal (estimated). End estimated. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: W. H. Davis shanty and redwood fence (NW cor. Montgomery & California)
shape_note: Davis bought lot 3 in '45 and 'built on it a wooden shanty and a red-wood fence. Mrs Montgomery occupied the house for a time in '45-6' (Bancroft v.679).

name: Frank Ward's house (SW cor. Sacramento & Montgomery)
shape_note: 'Lot 6 was bought by Wm M. Smith, who built in '47 or '48 a house occupied by his partner, Frank Ward, till '49' (Bancroft v.679). Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Dr John Townsend's house and office (California St)
shape_note: 'In 1847, Dr. John Townsend built his residence and physician's office on his fifty vara lot on the south side of California street between Montgomery and Sansome' (Eldredge ii.612 n.; Bancroft v.677: late '47). Sold to De Boom 1849. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Starkey, Janion & Co. store and office (Leidesdorff beach lot)
shape_note: 'Starkey, Janion & Co., merchants, had their store, with a separate office, on the Leidesdorff lot in '49-50. It was probably built in '48' (Bancroft v.677). Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Russ family's ship's caboose and additions - southern frontier of the town
shape_note: The Russ brothers (arrived on the Loo Choo, Mar 1847) 'put on the corner lot a ship's caboose, building additions as required'; until the gold fever 'the southern frontier of settlement', hidden by a high sand bank between Pine and California; later the Russ House site (Bancroft v.677). Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Wm Pettet's wooden store (Gelston & Co., furniture shops)
shape_note: Pettet's wooden building; Gelston & Co. (C. L. Ross) with the Whiton's cargo June 1847; Foster's furniture shop; McLean & Osburn Apr 1848 (Bancroft v.678). Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: McLean & Osburn's new wooden building near Montgomery & Sacramento
shape_note: 'Before the end of '48 McL. & O., or perhaps Osburn in company with Brannan, built a better wooden building west of the other, near the corner' (Bancroft v.678). Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Ward & Smith's large wooden store ('No. 3 Montgomery St')
shape_note: On the northern half of Spear's beach lot east of Montgomery between Clay and Washington, 1847-8; later Wells & Ward; the Star and Californian printed here end of 1848 (Bancroft v.680-681). Size and end estimated. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Sherman & Ruckel store (R. M. Sherman, W. H. Merrill builder)
shape_note: Southern half of the Spear beach lot bought late 1847; wooden store occupied 1848; Sherman 'had a bridge from his front door to the bank' (Bancroft v.681). Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Gelston & Co. / C. L. Ross 'New York Store' (NW cor. Washington & Montgomery)
shape_note: New building on the NW corner of Washington and Montgomery, where Chaplain Newell held the first recorded Protestant service on 25 Jul 1847; Ross's 'New York store' from Oct 1847, still his in 1849 (Eldredge ii.590; Bancroft v.683). Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: George Denike's bakery, saloon and (1848) hotel
shape_note: 'At c, on his own lot, Denike from '46 had a bakery, saloon, etc.' - scene of the 1847 Dornte murder; new hotel on the site advertised May 1848 (Bancroft v.684, block 34). Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Dickson & Hay 'Beehive' store
shape_note: Built 1847, advertised from Jan 1848 'as adjoining Ellis' and opposite Ross' lumber-yard' (Bancroft v.684). Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Vardeman Bennett groggery and bowling alley ('sailor's retreat')
shape_note: Opened early 1846, bowling alley added early 1847 (Brown 22b; Bancroft v.684, block 42); Bennett later refused to be 'swung' by O'Farrell's survey. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Thomas Smith saloon and bowling alley
shape_note: 'Smith also kept a saloon and bowling-alley at e on his own lot in '46-8' (Bancroft v.684). Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Marston's private school shanty (Dupont St, Broadway-Pacific)
shape_note: 'In April 1847, J. D. Marston opened a private school in a shanty on the west side of Dupont street between Broadway and Pacific' - 20-30 children, a few months (Eldredge ii.588; Annals 677). End estimated.

name: Francis Hoen and John Ellick houses
shape_note: 'Hoen and Ellick are remembered by Clark and Davis to have had houses in '46-8' (Bancroft v.685, block 43). Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: H. Harris house and Evans' slaughter-house
shape_note: 'An advertisement of '47 mentions "H. Harris' house" ... "Evans' slaughter-house" where Geo. Evans also lived' (Bancroft v.685, block 47). Block position per our reading of Bancroft's numbering (see notes). Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: W. H. Merrill's American House (boarding house)
shape_note: 'A kind of boarding establishment ... built in '47, a two-story wooden building'; new in Nov 1847 (Bancroft v.685-6, block 50). Brown places Merrill's boarding house on Powell St; block position uncertain. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Barton Mowry adobe (Mormon meeting room upstairs)
shape_note: 'Built in '47 an adobe house with wooden roof, for Mowry. The 2d floor was used by the Mormons for their meetings. This was one of the two old buildings that escaped the fires', still standing in 1867 (Bancroft v.686, block 51). Block position is our reading of Bancroft's numbering (see notes) - LOW.

name: A. A. Andrews house (W. H. Davis 1847-50; Nathan Spear died here)
shape_note: Andrews 'built a wooden house ... on the corner - where he lived from '45 to Nov. '47'; Davis bought it in '46 and lived there Nov 1847-1850 (Bancroft v.683, block 32; Brown 8a). Which corner is unknown. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: The windmill (landmark of 1846-47)
shape_note: 'On this lot also seems to have stood the windmill noted by several as a prominent landmark in '46-7. Piper says it had been built to grind wheat' (Bancroft v.684); the Star office moved in Feb 1848 'within a stone's-throw of the old windmill'; the Aug 1847 business census lists '2 mills (horse and wind)'. Form (post or smock mill) and height ESTIMATED.

name: William Glover house (Mormon colonist)
shape_note: 'Wm Glover built a house and lived on his lot at e' (Bancroft v.682, block 26); Brown 13a instead has Glover in a small dilapidated frame house on John Cooper's lots. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Brannan's California Star office (moved Feb 1848)
shape_note: Star office moved Feb 1848 'about 100 varas up Washington St., within a stone's-throw of the old windmill', probably to Brannan's own lot (Bancroft v.682). Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Robert A. Parker's two-storey store on Clay St ('opposite the Portsmouth House')
shape_note: 'Robert A. Parker moved in his new store, a two-story building on Clay street, in March 1848. On the same lot, where the Old Mill House stood' (Brown); free grog at the sign-raising (Bancroft v.681). End = fire of 24 Dec 1849 (estimated). Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Paty's adobe (built by Benito Diaz)
shape_note: 'At n was Paty's adobe, probably built by Benito Diaz about '40, and sold to Capt. Paty in '47'; McDonald & Buchanan auctioneers here Jan-May 1848 (Bancroft v.681-2, block 24). Position in the block and dates uncertain. Block/lot after Bancroft v.676-686 ('San Francisco and its buildings before ... May 1848').

name: Wm Stout house
shape_note: Brooklyn colonist (arrived 31 Jul 1846). Located from William Glover's 1885 supplementary statement, compiled from nine members of the Mormon colony (Bancroft v.686 'Additions'). Position within the block, size and end ESTIMATED (shanty or small frame house).

shape_note: Brooklyn colonist (arrived 31 Jul 1846). Located from William Glover's 1885 supplementary statement, compiled from nine members of the Mormon colony (Bancroft v.686 'Additions'). Position within the block, size and end ESTIMATED (shanty or small frame house).

shape_note: Brooklyn colonist (arrived 31 Jul 1846). Located from William Glover's 1885 supplementary statement, compiled from nine members of the Mormon colony (Bancroft v.686 'Additions'). Position within the block, size and end ESTIMATED (shanty or small frame house).

name: John Joyce house
shape_note: Brooklyn colonist (arrived 31 Jul 1846). Located from William Glover's 1885 supplementary statement, compiled from nine members of the Mormon colony (Bancroft v.686 'Additions'). Position within the block, size and end ESTIMATED (shanty or small frame house).

name: Brooklyn Mormon colonists' tent camp among the sand hills
shape_note: ~230-240 colonists landed 31 Jul 1846 and 'immediately set up their tents among the sand-hills close to the beach' (Annals 186); 'camped for a time on the beach and the vacant lots', then some went to Marin as lumbermen, some wintered in Richardson's casa grande or the old mission buildings (Eldredge ii.543). Count (~6 per tent) and centre ESTIMATED.

name: Fort Montgomery battery at Clark's Point (the 'battery' of Battery St)
shape_note: Begun about 17 Jul 1846 by Lt. Misroon's sailors: 'High on the steep bluff facing the bay Misroon excavated a terrace whereon he mounted a battery of five guns'; gave its name to Battery St; existed until fall 1849 (Eldredge ii.542-543); 'between Battery St and the water, at the foot of the hill', the block north of Clark's warehouse (Bancroft v.685). MATERIAL: earth terrace/earthwork, not adobe. Size estimated.

name: W. S. Clark's warehouse at the foot of Broadway
shape_note: Clark (who gave his name to Clark's Point) built a warehouse in '47-8 on the lot he still owned in 1885; 'new warehouse at foot of Broadway at the stone pier' to let, Mar 1848 (Bancroft v.685). Size and end estimated.

name: Clark's wharf / Broadway pier at Clark's Point (the landing place)
shape_note: 'The principal landing place was at the Punta del Embarcadero, or Clark's Point - now the corner of Broadway and Battery ... William S. Clark built in 1847 a small wharf at the point', piles driven with a 1,200-lb pig-iron monkey; first vessel to dock: brig Belfast, Oct 1848. Council authorized a 150-ft Broadway pier in Oct 1847 (Eldredge ii.573). Length estimated (~150 ft); deck height above sea level.

name: Little pier at the foot of Clay Street (and the 1847-48 extension)
shape_note: 'At the foot of Clay street a little pier had been built at which small boats could land at high tide'; Oct 1847 the council authorized a 547-ft extension ($11,000); work stopped Jan 1848 when funds ran out (Eldredge ii.573); 'nobody remembers that the result was of any practical use' (Bancroft v.679). Built length ESTIMATED.

name: B. R. Buckelew's watchmaker's shop and dwelling at 'the Point'
shape_note: 'A man by the name of Bucklow, in 1848 built a dwelling and store on a piece of land, known as the Point' (Brown); advertised from Apr 1847 (Bancroft v.684). Position estimated (Buckelew's Point, Sansome & Pacific).

name: Other houses and shanties of Yerba Buena, mid-1846 (unlocated)
shape_note: By mid-summer 1846 'buildings of all kinds had increased to nearly fifty' (Annals 173); Bancroft (v.676) locates only about half of all structures. This group tops the located rows up to ~50; adobe and frame mixed. Count ESTIMATED.

name: Unlocated frame houses, adobes and shanties of 1847 (plaza and Stockton slopes)
shape_note: 79 buildings on 1 Apr 1847 (31 frame, 26 adobe, 22 shanties); 78 more by the end of August (47 frame, 11 adobe, 20 shanties) = 157 (Gilbert in the Star, Aug-Sep 1847; Annals 173; Bancroft v.647). Located rows cover ~80; this group and the next supply the rest. Count ESTIMATED.

name: Unlocated frame houses and shanties of 1847 (Montgomery St beach to Clark's Point)
shape_note: See previous row; 'Fifty houses built in the last month' (Star, 17 Apr 1847). Count ESTIMATED.

name: Unlocated buildings added before the gold rush, spring 1848
shape_note: By the end of April 1848 'nearly two hundred buildings, viz.: one hundred and thirty-five finished dwelling-houses, ten unfinished ..., twelve stores and warehouses, and thirty-five shanties' (Annals 174); 192 buildings (Californian, 20 Apr 1848). Count ESTIMATED.

name: Parker House hotel (Kearny St facing the plaza)
shape_note: 'A certain two story frame building, known as the "Parker House," ... on Kearny street, facing the plaza', rents $120,000 a year, gamblers on the whole second floor (Annals 254); built 1849 by R. A. Parker and J. H. Brown; burned 24 Dec 1849 and rebuilt (burned twice more in 1850; later the Jenny Lind Theatre site) (Eldredge ii.592); it stood on Sherreback's old 50-vara lot with the El Dorado (Brown 5a). Size estimated.

name: El Dorado gambling saloon (canvas tent), SE cor. Washington & Kearny
shape_note: 'The "El Dorado," a gambling saloon, which adjoined the Parker House on the right, at the corner of Washington street, and which was only a canvas tent of moderate size, brought at the rate of forty thousand dollars per annum' (Annals 254); on Sherreback's old lot; burned 24 Dec 1849. Size estimated.

name: St. Francis Hotel (four storeys), SW corner Clay & Dupont
shape_note: 'The St. Francis hotel, a four story building, stood on the southwest corner of Clay and Dupont streets, on the lot whereon Jacob P. Leese erected the first house' (Eldredge ii.593). Opening date (late 1849), size and end ESTIMATED.

name: Storeship Niantic (beached hulk), NW corner Clay & Sansome
shape_note: Brought ~250 Argonauts from Panama in 1849, beached and 'covered with a shingle roof, sub-divided into stores and offices' (Kelly, in Eldredge ii.579-580); burned in the fire of 3-4 May 1851; Niantic Hotel later on the site. Hull size estimated (vessel of ~1,000 tons per Kelly).

name: Storeships General Harrison (Clay & Battery) and Apollo (Sacramento & Battery)
shape_note: 'On the northwest corner of Clay and Battery streets was the General Harrison. The Apollo was on the northwest corner of Sacramento and Battery' - all burned in the fire of May 1851 (Eldredge ii.579). Two hulls ~100 m apart along Battery St; beaching dates and sizes ESTIMATED.

name: Central Wharf (Long Wharf), first 800 ft
shape_note: Begun May 1849 'from the bank in the middle of the block between Sacramento and Clay streets, where Leidesdorff street now is'; 800 ft finished by Dec 1849; 35 ft wide; reached 2,000 ft (Drumm St) by Oct 1850; buildings on piles along both sides; became Commercial St as the cove was filled (Eldredge ii.573-574; Annals 291). Footprint = the 1849 extent; point = its centre.

name: Signal station on Telegraph Hill (Loma Alta)
shape_note: 'Early in 1849 this enterprising firm [Sweeny & Baugh] had erected a station-house on Telegraph Hill' signalling ship arrivals with semaphore arms (Annals 465), giving the hill its name (Eldredge ii.577). Add a tall mast with semaphore arms. Size and end ESTIMATED.

name: Happy Valley tent city (First-Second, Market-Mission)
shape_note: 'Sheltered from the harsh winds, tents had been set up and the place named Happy valley. This was between First, Second, Market, and Mission streets ... contained, in the winter of 1849-50, about one thousand tents' (Eldredge ii.593). End estimated.

name: Pleasant Valley tents (south of Mission St to Howard)
shape_note: 'To the south as far as Howard street, was Pleasant valley' (Eldredge ii.593). Count ESTIMATED.

name: Sydney Town tents and shanties at the foot of Telegraph Hill
shape_note: 'The tents dotting the hills in the rear and spreading around the base of Telegraph hill to the north. This region ... bore the significant title of Sidney Town' (Eldredge ii.593). Count ESTIMATED; mixed tents and board shanties.

name: Little Chile (Chilecito) tents and houses, Kearny-Stockton, Broadway-Green
shape_note: 'Reaching from Kearny to Stockton streets, between Broadway and Green street, was Little Chili, where the Chilenos and Peruanos were gathered' (Eldredge ii.593); the Hounds wrecked its 'tents and houses' on 15 Jul 1849 (ii.594). Count ESTIMATED.

name: Spring Valley tents (Powell-Mason, Washington-Broadway)
shape_note: 'Westerly between Powell and Mason streets, Washington street and Broadway, was Spring valley' (Eldredge ii.593). Count ESTIMATED.

name: Laundry tents at Washerwoman's Lagoon (Laguna Pequena)
shape_note: In 1849 washermen 'established themselves' at the pond 'with their tents for ironing, their large kettles for boiling the clothes and their fluted washboards along the edge of the water'; gardeners on the black loam around it (Eldredge ii.615-616). Place tents around (not in) the lagoon. Count ESTIMATED.

name: Miners' tents and gardens along Mission Creek (winter 1849-50)
shape_note: Bayard Taylor (1849): 'Several former miners in anticipation of a great influx of emigrants in the spring, pitched their tents on the best spots along Mission creek and began preparing the ground for gardens' (Eldredge i.330). Count ESTIMATED.
